title: Istanbul Art Exhibitions in November–December 2026: What’s On, Until When, and How to Group Them
excerpt: Seven verified exhibitions at Istanbul Modern, Sakıp Sabancı, Pera, Zeyrek Çinili Hamam and the Digital Experience Center, ordered by closing date and grouped by neighbourhood.

body.text: If you are in Istanbul in November or December 2026, the city’s private museums and a few unusual venues have a strong overlapping programme — but the shows close on different dates and sit in neighbourhoods that are far apart. This guide lists what we could confirm on each venue’s own website on 26 October 2026, the stated closing date, and a way to group the visits by area so you do not spend a day crossing the city for a single gallery. Opening hours, closing days and programmes change, so treat every date here as a starting point and re-check it on the venue page before you go.
The calendar at a glance: what closes first

items: Until 22 November 2026 — [Semiha Berksoy: Aria of All Colors](https://www.istanbulmodern.org/en/exhibitions/semiha-berksoy-aria-of-all-colors), Istanbul Modern (Karaköy/Tophane). The museum presents more than 200 works covering her career across opera and theatre, painting, film and literature.

Until 27 December 2026 — [Yoko Ono: Insound and Instructure](https://sakipsabancimuzesi.org/en/sergiler-ve-etkinlikler/sergi/78), Sakıp Sabancı Museum (Emirgan). 67 works from the late 1950s onward, spread across two lower galleries, the garden and the Atlı Köşk.

Until 31 January 2027 — [Frank Bowling: Creation and Destruction](https://peramuseum.org/exhibition/frank-bowling-creation-and-destruction-/1324), Pera Museum (Tepebaşı, Beyoğlu), with works by Francis Bacon and Victor Willing as “interruptions”.

Until 31 January 2027 — [Alex Červený: Atlas of Encounters](https://zeyrekcinilihamam.com/en/alex-cervenys-first-solo-exhibition-in-turkiye-atlas-of-encounters-opens-at-zeyrek-cinili-hamam), in the Byzantine cistern beneath Zeyrek Çinili Hamam (Zeyrek, Fatih).
Until 28 March 2027 — The Republic Behind the Scenes, early-Republic press photography of Istanbul daily life, also at the [Pera Museum](https://www.peramuseum.org/exhibitions/upcoming-exhibitions).

No closing date published — [Beneath the Same Blue](https://www.istanbulmodern.org/en/press-releases/istanbul-modern-presents-beneath-the-same-blue-a-new-interpretation-of-its-coll), Istanbul Modern’s collection exhibition, opened 8 September 2026 across all four floors.

No closing date published — [Dalí Cybernetics](https://kultur.istanbul/salvador-dalinin-sira-disi-dunyasi-istanbulda-kapilarini-acti/), an immersive digital show that opened on 22 October 2026 at Kültür AŞ’s Digital Experience Center (Sütlüce, Beyoğlu).

body.text: The practical consequence: if your trip falls in the second half of November, put Istanbul Modern first, because the Berksoy exhibition is the earliest to close. If you arrive in late December, the Yoko Ono show in Emirgan is the one with a hard deadline; everything else on this list continues into 2027 or has no announced end.

Most venues here state that they are closed on Mondays: the Sakıp Sabancı Museum, the Pera Museum, Zeyrek Çinili Hamam and the Digital Experience Center all say so on their own pages. We did not confirm Istanbul Modern’s current hours for this article, so check its visitor page. In practice, keep Monday for mosques, bazaars, walks or a Bosphorus ferry, and schedule galleries from Tuesday to Sunday. Pera’s page lists a late opening until 22:00 on Fridays, which makes it a good evening option.
Grouping 1: Karaköy/Tophane and Tepebaşı in one day

Istanbul Modern on the Karaköy waterfront and the Pera Museum in Tepebaşı are both in Beyoğlu and are the easiest pair to combine. With two large exhibitions at Istanbul Modern (the collection show fills the building, and Berksoy alone has more than 200 works) it is realistic to give it a full morning, then go uphill to Pera for the afternoon. Pera has two different shows — painting in the Bowling exhibition and archive photography in The Republic Behind the Scenes — so decide in advance which one is your priority if your energy is limited. On a Friday you can reverse the order and finish at Pera in the evening.
Grouping 2: Emirgan as a Bosphorus half-day

The Sakıp Sabancı Museum sits far up the European shore of the Bosphorus, so treat it as its own half-day rather than an add-on. The Yoko Ono exhibition extends outdoors into the garden, which is worth knowing on a cold or wet December day: dress for some time outside. Combining it with a walk along the Bosphorus shore or lunch in the village area keeps the journey worthwhile. The museum lists its hours as 10:00–18:00, closed Mondays.
Grouping 3: Zeyrek, Fatih and the Golden Horn

Zeyrek Çinili Hamam is on the historic peninsula, which makes it easy to fit into a day you already plan around old Istanbul. The Červený exhibition is installed in the cistern beneath the hammam, and the venue states that admission is free and that it opens 10:00–18:00 except Mondays. If you are drawn to the immersive Dalí show, the Digital Experience Center is across the Golden Horn in Sütlüce, next to Miniatürk, so a Zeyrek morning followed by a Sütlüce afternoon is a sensible combination by taxi. Kültür AŞ notes that weekday mornings until about 14:00 can be busy with school groups, so independent visitors may prefer later in the day. The centre’s own page says tickets are sold at the entrance kiosk or through Passo.
How to choose if you only have one or two days

items: One day, contemporary and modern art focus: Istanbul Modern in the morning, Pera in the afternoon.
One day, a single big name: the Yoko Ono exhibition in Emirgan, plus the Bosphorus shore.
Travelling with children or teenagers: the Dalí show’s VR and interactive sections are designed for participation; pair it with Zeyrek if you want something quieter afterwards.
Interested in Istanbul’s own history: The Republic Behind the Scenes at Pera and the Ottoman astronomy pages reworked in Červený’s cistern installation.
Open each venue’s page on the day before your visit to confirm hours, any holiday closures and whether the exhibition is still on.

Do not rely on a museum pass for these private venues without checking coverage; our guide on [museum pass versus single tickets](/blog/istanbul-museum-pass-or-single-tickets) explains how to compare.
If you need step-free routes, seating or sensory information, our [museum access planning checklist](/blog/istanbul-museum-access-planning-checklist) lists the questions to send ahead.
For the rest of your stay, see our [3, 5 or 7-day Istanbul itinerary](/blog/istanbul-itinerary-3-5-7-days) and the [winter travel guide to Türkiye](/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).

body.text: We have not listed ticket prices because they were not part of what we verified and change frequently. If you would like your exhibition days built into a private Istanbul programme with transfers between neighbourhoods, see our [tourism services](/services/tourism) or [contact us](/contact).

seo.intent: Find out which major Istanbul exhibitions are open in November–December 2026, when each closes, and how to combine them by area.
seo.uniqueValue: A closing-date-ordered calendar of seven exhibitions verified on venue sites on 26 October 2026, with Monday-closure warnings and neighbourhood pairings, rather than a general museum list.

quality.reviewNotes: Prepared 2026-10-26. Venue-owned pages opened 2026-10-26: Istanbul Modern (Berksoy 22 Jan–22 Nov 2026, 200+ works; Beneath the Same Blue opened 8 Sep, 230 works, four floors, no end date stated), Sakıp Sabancı Museum (Yoko Ono 25 Jun–27 Dec 2026, 67 works, galleries/garden/Atlı Köşk, 10:00–18:00 closed Mon), Pera Museum (Bowling 29 Sep 2026–31 Jan 2027; Republic Behind the Scenes to 28 Mar 2027; closed Mon, Fri to 22:00), Zeyrek Çinili Hamam (Červený 24 Sep 2026–31 Jan 2027, cistern, free, 10:00–18:00 except Mon), kultur.istanbul (Dalí Cybernetics opened 22 Oct 2026, Passo, no end date; DDM Sütlüce next to Miniatürk, 10:00–18:00 closed Mon, school groups weekdays to 14:00). Istanbul Modern hours not verified. Arter show dropped: arter.org.tr blocked fetching, end date unverifiable. Neighbourhood grouping and timing advice are editorial. No prices except stated free entry. Independent review 2026-10-26: all eight cited URLs re-opened and every end date, opening date and Monday closure re-checked (all match; Istanbul Modern hours still unconfirmed and framed as such); removed the unsupported “retrospective” label for Berksoy and attributed Passo ticketing to the Digital Experience Center page rather than the Dalí article.
